Every row is a claim the Colorado State University Extension page supports (opened in full by the Social Media chat and the box writer; reviewed July 2024): leaves as mulch insulate tender or newly planted plants; leaves in garden beds are organic matter; tree leaves go in compost; mowing leaves into the lawn adds organic matter to the soil over time; mow with the deck on its highest setting. Not on the page and therefore left out: trees or shrubs mulching, a blanket on the roots, a thick pile smothering the lawn. The Minnesota page was not available. No figure, no price, no forecast, no professional line (the card is yard leaves, not trade work).
headline:
Fallen Leaves Make Free Mulch
Mow Them, Don't Bag Them
titan_line: Echo, if you don't want to rake, just run the mower over the leaves. Set it on its highest setting, and chopped leaves are useful around the yard.
rows: Mulch: use chopped leaves in garden beds and around young plants.
In the cold they help protect young or tender plants.
Compost: chopped leaves are a good addition to a compost pile.
Soil: as they break down, chopped leaves add organic matter to the soil.
echo_line: Mulch, compost and richer soil. Those leaves work harder than I do.
source: Colorado State University Extension, Using Leaves in the Landscape, reviewed July 2024 · read Oct 30, 2026
disclaimer: General home information. Check your own yard and mower before you start.
